newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan shinkin banks mull Musashino bailout plan.
newsitem.headline: Japan shinkin banks mull Musashino bailout plan.

text.p: Japan's "shinkin" banks are working out a programme to bail out Tokyo-based Musashino Shinkin Bank, which is reeling under problem loans now estimated at about 39 billion yen, industry sources said on Wednesday.

Under the programme, Zenshinren Bank, a national association of credit associations, and 50 Tokyo-based shinkin banks are expected to provide aid to Musashino, along with funds from the industry's mutual assistance system, they said.
Shinkin banks are small credit associations which take deposits and lend mainly to members and are supervised by the Ministry of Finance (MOF).
Zenshinren Bank said late on Monday that it would bail out Musashino, which announced earlier that day that it was facing financial problems and had given up efforts to restructure on its own.
Zenshinren initially wanted Johnan Shinkin Bank, Japan's biggest credit association, to merge with Musashino, but Johnan rejected the rescue proposal, the sources said.

Under the programme now being worked out, Musashino's problem loans will be separated from healthy loans and those problem loans will be taken care of through financial aid provided by Zenshinren and other shinkin banks, they said.
